notes: findHover (Handler.ts): the direct walk first (setHoverTarget over the whole display list, top first). Only when it found no target and _pointerSize is truthy: candidates = every element of the display list, top first, not ignored, without ignoreCoarsePointer (nor a parent with it), whose box (getBoundingRect through its transform) intersects the pointer rect (x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size) -- silent ones included. Then for r = 0; r < size / 2; r += 4 and theta = 0; theta < 2 PI; theta += PI / 12: setHoverTarget(candidates, x + r cos theta, y + r sin theta) -- which walks the candidates from the END of the array, i.e. BOTTOM first -- and the first sample with a target ends the search.

init: useCoarsePointer defaults to 'auto' (echarts: root.__ECHARTS__DEFAULT__COARSE_POINTER may change the default); 'auto' or null means env.touchEventsSupported ('ontouchstart' in window, not IE / old Edge); a boolean otherwise. pointerSize = retrieve2(opts.pointerSize, 44) only when it is on; the handler tests it for truthiness, so 0 (and NaN) is off. Large series (bar, candlestick, lines, scatter batches) set ignoreCoarsePointer.

createRepaintRects (canvas/Layer.ts): null on the layer's first paint. Otherwise, for each element of this frame's list (the layer's range): shouldPaint = shouldBePainted(w, h, true, true); the previous paint rect joins the pool when it was rendered and (dirty or not to be painted); the current paint rect joins when it is to be painted and (dirty or not rendered). Then for each element of the previous list (the previous range) that is not to be painted or no longer in storage but was rendered: its previous rect. A rect joins only when finite and not zero (width or height exactly 0). Pool: the first rect starts it; a rect is merged (union) into the FIRST pool rect it intersects (edges touching count); once the pool reached maxRepaintRectCount (5) it is "full" and a rect that meets none is merged into the rect whose union grows the least (area of union - both areas; the first of equals); otherwise it starts a new pool rect. Finally a loop merges any two pool rects that intersect (dropping zero ones) until none do.

getPaintRect (Displayable.ts): the box (getBoundingRect -- for a path the path box grown by the line width when stroked, by max(lineWidth, strokeContainThreshold 5) when it has no fill; through the transform), grown by the shadow (width += 2 blur + |offsetX|, x = min(x, x + offsetX - blur), likewise y), then when not zero: x = floor(x - tolerance), y = floor(y - tolerance), width = ceil(width + 1 + 2 tolerance), height likewise. tolerance is 0, 10 for a TSpan.

Bookkeeping (Painter._paintPerCursorInRect / graphic.brush): with rects, each rect clips and every element of the list whose CURRENT paint rect intersects it is brushed and gets setPrevPaintRect(paint rect); a brushed element that is not to be painted is marked not rendered. On a full paint (no rects -- the first frame) elements are brushed WITHOUT setPrevPaintRect, so an element painted only in full frames has no previous rect: moving it later adds only its new rect (case move-after-full) and its old pixels stay on the canvas.
An empty array (nothing dirty but the layer flagged) paints nothing; a frame with no dirty element and a clean layer never calls createRepaintRects (case nothing).

dirty.note: a bar restyled and back: the first change has no previous rect (painted only in the full frame)
moving an element painted only in the full frame: upstream adds the new rect only (its old pixels stay)
a second move: the old and the new rect
two changed elements whose rects overlap become one
rects that only touch are merged: intersect counts the edge
four disjoint changes: four rects
five: the pool is full after the fifth
six: the sixth merges into the rect it grows least
twelve small changes on two rows merged into five
a removed element: its previous rect from the previous list
an added element: its rect, never rendered
ignore on: the previous rect only; off again: the current rect
opacity 0 is not painted
stroke widths, stroke without fill (strokeContainThreshold 5), shadows
circles at fractional centres
rects that only meet after merging: the final pass joins them
a z2 change marks the element dirty: one rect, whatever the order
a frame where nothing changed: no rects computed
the pool full, a sixth rect half way between two: the union grows the same with either, the first one takes it

invisible written straight onto an element (no markRedraw, not dirty; unlike ignore it stays in the display list) while another changes: its previous rect because it is not to be painted (and, its rect the first, brushed there: not rendered any more); shown again the same way: its current rect because it was not rendered

guards.note: theta += PI / 12 accumulates below 2 PI after 24 steps: 25 samples a ring
r < 22.5: still six rings
r < 4: one ring
r < 4.5: two rings
ring 0 asks the same point 25 times
'auto' without touch events: no pointer size
useCoarsePointer false: no pointer size
pointerSize 0 is kept but falsy: never a fallback
the default pointer size
a point 10 px off a 4 px symbol: found only by the fallback
23 px off: a candidate, but r < 22 never reaches
on both symbols: the top one
off both: the candidates are walked bottom first
5 px off both: no direct hit, the bottom one by the rings
a 1 px line 12 px away: found by the fallback
the first frame paints everything
no dirty element, a clean layer: createRepaintRects is not called
an element moved after only a full frame: the new rect alone
a second move: old and new
overlapping rects merge
touching rects merge (two left of three)
four disjoint: four
five disjoint: five
six disjoint: still five
twelve: at most five
the final pass joins what merging made meet
a filled node with no stroke: hit on its shape, not 3 px off it
3 px off a node: the fallback finds it
a tree node: its ring and border by half their width
a radar ring: max(lineWidth, 5) / 2 either side
a radar symbol: its shape; the fallback finds it 2 px off
a graph node: its border by half its width
a filled node with a 1 px border: half its width, not the threshold
